intended_object: The antipode of the descended Hopf algebra: the k-subalgebra of L[M] made of elements fixed by the simultaneous Galois action on coefficients and exponents is preserved by the antipode (a·m ↦ a·(−m)), and the restriction is an involutive k-algebra automorphism. Inferred from the docstring and the module documentation (Galois descent of split tori / diagonalizable groups, Milne Thm 12.23).
explanation: The body takes the group-algebra antipode on MonoidAlgebra L (Multiplicative M), views it over k (restrictScalars k), composes it with the inclusion of the invariant subalgebra and restricts the target back to that subalgebra. The restriction is valid because the antipode commutes with the Galois action, so it keeps invariant elements invariant. The group algebra is commutative, so the antipode is an algebra map. It is also its own inverse (antipode_antipode), so building an AlgEquiv with the same map in both directions is correct. The companion lemma groupAlgebraInvariantsAntipode_apply confirms it acts by the ordinary antipode. Fields k and L with L/k Galois are the natural setting for this Galois-descent construction. Mathlib has no general version of this object.
